The Best Luxury Hotels in Egypt, City by City

The luxury hotels our private Egypt journeys use in Cairo, Aswan, Abu Simbel, the Red Sea, Alexandria and Siwa, and what is happening in Luxor until July 2027

23 November 2026 · 10 minute read

By Islam Hussein, Sillage Égypte journey designer. Last updated: November 2026.

The quick answer

The best luxury hotel in Egypt depends on the morning you want. These are the hotels our journeys use, as of November 2026:

  • Cairo: the Four Seasons First Residence, the Four Seasons Nile Plaza or the St. Regis on the river, and the Marriott Mena House at the foot of the Giza plateau.
  • Luxor: the Winter Palace is closed for restoration and reported to reopen in July 2027 as a Mandarin Oriental. Your Luxor hotel is named in your proposal.
  • Aswan: the Mandarin Oriental, the former Old Cataract, with the Palace Wing open while the Nile Wing is renovated.
  • Abu Simbel: Seti Abu Simbel Lake Resort or Azal Lagoon Resort, chosen for the setting, not the polish.
  • Red Sea: the Oberoi Sahl Hasheesh.
  • Alexandria and Siwa: the Four Seasons at San Stefano, and Adrère Amellal, which has no electricity at all.

Every search for the best luxury hotels in Egypt is really a question about where to wake up: beside the pyramids, above the Nile, at the edge of the sea. Sillage Égypte (sillage-egypte.com), the private Egypt journey designer, owns none of these hotels. They are independent suppliers, which is why we can be plain about them. What follows is the list of hotels our published journeys use, what each is for, and when it is the wrong answer. The Egyptian hotel map is changing quickly, with the Winter Palace closed, the Old Cataract partly under renovation and part of the Mena House out of service, so confirm the specifics before you plan around a particular wing.

Cairo: three hotels on the river, one beside the pyramids

Choose by the Cairo you want. For city evenings, sleep on the river; for the plateau at first light, sleep at the Mena House. Several of our journeys do both.

On the river. The Four Seasons First Residence stands on the Nile's west bank in Giza, bordered by the zoological gardens, and it opens Cairo, Two Views and Beyond the Nile. The Four Seasons Nile Plaza is a Nile-front tower in Garden City, and it begins The Complete Egypt. The St. Regis is on the Nile Corniche, and it begins The Nile & the Red Sea. All three put you on the river in the city rather than out at the plateau, which suits a first night and a day of Cairo proper.

At the plateau. The Marriott Mena House has been a hotel since 1886, at the foot of the Giza plateau. The historic Palace Wing is reported closed long-term, and Pyramid-view rooms are now sold in the garden wing, so the old advice to ask for the old building no longer applies. We ask for a Pyramid-view room; it is requested, not promised. The Grand Egyptian Museum is also at Giza, so hotel, museum and monuments now share the same end of Cairo.

Honest counsel: Giza is not central Cairo, and an evening in Zamalek or Islamic Cairo from the Mena House means a drive. That is why the longer journeys split the stay. For the plateau itself, The Empty Plateau is two hours at Giza, at dawn or before sunset, opened for your party alone, with staff and guards remaining, subject to official permission for the date. More on the city in the Cairo destination guide.

Luxor: the Winter Palace, and what happens until July 2027

Luxor's famous address is the Winter Palace, which opened in 1907. It is closed for restoration and is reported to reopen in July 2027 as a Mandarin Oriental. Until it reopens, we will not promise you a room in it.

Your Luxor hotel is named in your proposal, with the current position of the hotel checked for your dates. On The Nile & the Red Sea and Beyond the Nile, you reach Luxor aboard the Oberoi Zahra. Either way, a morning on the west bank works best when your Egyptologist times the crossing before the coaches. More in the Luxor destination guide.

Aswan: the Mandarin Oriental, the former Old Cataract

Aswan's address is the Old Cataract, which opened in January 1900 and has been a Mandarin Oriental since 1 May 2026. It is the hotel most associated with Agatha Christie, whose name stays with it. The Grand Tour, The Complete Egypt and Christmas & New Year on the Nile all use it.

The Palace Wing is open while the Nile Wing is renovated, with the work running to July 2027. So the room we ask for is in the Palace Wing, and it is requested, not promised.

Tea on the Terrace is the Aswan experience built for the slowest hour of the day. More in the Aswan destination guide.

Abu Simbel: a lake resort, chosen for the setting

Abu Simbel has very few rooms, and that is the reason to stay. The Grand Tour uses Seti Abu Simbel Lake Resort and Christmas & New Year on the Nile uses Azal Lagoon Resort. Both are chosen for the setting, not for polish, so expect a lake resort rather than a palace. Abu Simbel is always reached by air on a Sillage journey, never by the long desert road. More in the Abu Simbel guide.

The Red Sea: the Oberoi Sahl Hasheesh

Our Red Sea address is the Oberoi Sahl Hasheesh, an all-suite resort south of Hurghada. The Nile & the Red Sea gives it four nights after four on the river, reached by road from Luxor in four to five hours, with a flight from Hurghada to Cairo afterwards.

Honest counsel: you come for water and quiet, not for a town, and the order matters. The sea is the right shape after the monuments, not before them. Hurghada's sea is reported at about 21 to 23 °C in winter and 27 °C in October. More in the Hurghada destination guide.

Alexandria and Siwa: the two ends of Beyond the Nile

Beyond the Nile pairs the most polished hotel on this list with the least, and that contrast is the point of the journey.

Alexandria. The Four Seasons Alexandria at San Stefano is on the Mediterranean side of the city, a modern international hotel rather than a period piece. More in the Alexandria destination guide.

Siwa. Adrère Amellal, reached along the coast, is built of salt and mud at the foot of the White Mountain. It has no electricity and is lit by candles after dark. It is rustic, and it is the wrong answer for anyone who wants a spa and a signal. The UK excepts Siwa town and the Marsa Matruh to Siwa road from its wider warning on the Western Desert, while the US is reported to list the Western Desert as Do Not Travel, so read your own government's advice first.

The river: the nights with no hotel

Some of the best beds in Egypt are not in hotels. The Complete Egypt spends five nights on a private dahabiya from Esna to Aswan, and Christmas & New Year on the Nile charters one for six. The Nile & the Red Sea and Beyond the Nile use the Oberoi Zahra between Aswan and Luxor, for four and six nights. On those nights the boat is the room, and all you decide is the deck chair.

How we choose the luxury hotels in your journey

Four tests, in order. Position at the hours that matter: near what you will do at the hour you will do it. Setting over polish, where the setting is itself the sight. The specific room: wings, floors and views decide more of a stay than the brand on the letterhead, so we request categories, not merely hotels, though a room type is requested, not promised. And the swap test: every journey is private, there are no scheduled groups, and when a better fit exists for your dates, we say so and move.

Every hotel is named in your proposal, never "a five-star hotel or similar", and any of them can be swapped to suit while we refine it. A last note on the word best: it lasts exactly as long as the room you are in.

FAQ

What are the best luxury hotels in Egypt? The ones our journeys use are the Four Seasons First Residence, the Four Seasons Nile Plaza, the St. Regis and the Marriott Mena House in Cairo; the Mandarin Oriental (Old Cataract) in Aswan; the Oberoi Sahl Hasheesh on the Red Sea; the Four Seasons at San Stefano in Alexandria; and Adrère Amellal at Siwa. In Luxor, the Winter Palace is reported to reopen in July 2027, and your hotel is named in your proposal.

Should I stay near the pyramids or in central Cairo? Stay at the Mena House if your Cairo is the plateau and the Grand Egyptian Museum. Stay on the river if your Cairo is evenings in the city. The Complete Egypt and The Nile & the Red Sea do both, and the proposal will say which your dates suit.

Is the Winter Palace open? No. It is closed for restoration and is reported to reopen in July 2027 as a Mandarin Oriental. We do not promise a stay there before it reopens.

Are these hotels suitable for families? Tell us the children's ages and how your family sleeps, and the hotels in your proposal are chosen with that in mind. Adrère Amellal, with no electricity, is the one to think hardest about.

Does Sillage Égypte own any of these hotels? No. Sillage owns none of its hotels, boats or restaurants; each is an independent supplier, named in your proposal, and swapped to suit whenever a better fit exists. What Sillage runs is the journey itself: private throughout, your own car, your own certified Egyptologist.

What do these hotels cost per night? We do not publish nightly rates. Hotels are included in the journey price, which runs from €2,190 to €11,650 per person for two or more travellers, and your proposal prices the exact rooms on your dates. The price is fixed once confirmed in writing, except for government action, taxes and fees, or significant currency changes.

When should I book these hotels? In our experience: Christmas and New Year nine to twelve months ahead, Easter six to nine months, high winter four to six months, the shoulder months three to six months, and summer six to ten weeks. The takeaway

Egypt's best luxury hotels are not a ranking but a set of positions: sleep by the Nile in Cairo, beside the plateau at Giza, above the river at Aswan, at the water's edge on the Red Sea, and by candlelight at Siwa. In each, ask for the room, not only the hotel, and until mid-2027 ask us what is open.
